module.title: Defensive Code & Exceptions
module.subtitle: Guard clauses, raising clear errors, and avoiding silent try/except traps
lesson_points: Validate bad inputs right at the top of a function (guard clauses) and fail loudly with a clear exception like ValueError.
Only catch specific exceptions you genuinely know how to recover from (except ValueError:), never a bare 'except:' that hides bugs.
Stepping through try/except shows execution jumping straight from the failing line to the matching except block.

quizzes.title: Tracing a Caught Exception
quizzes.explanation: int('abc') raises ValueError on line 3, skipping line 4 and jumping straight to 'except ValueError:' which returns -1.

quizzes.title: Spot the Swallowed Bug
quizzes.prompt: Click the line that dangerously hides typos and real bugs by catching EVERY possible error silently.
quizzes.explanation: A bare 'except:' on line 4 catches KeyError, NameError typos, and even KeyboardInterrupt silently—catch specific errors like KeyError instead.

quizzes.title: Why Fail Loudly?
quizzes.prompt: Why is raising ValueError on invalid inputs often safer than quietly returning 0?
quizzes.sample_explanation: Quietly returning 0 hides mistakes and lets corrupt data keep flowing, whereas raising an error stops immediately where the bug happened.
quizzes.explanation: Failing loudly surfaces invalid state at the exact source instead of letting subtle bugs corrupt downstream calculations.
